subject: Prompt/Response attribution and subprocessor dataflow map
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@medscale.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medscale.ai, samir@medscale.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify attribution + subprocessor map for DPA review

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal at MedScale is trying to close DPA language this week and had two high-priority asks I wanted to surface:

1) Attribution / ownership: our counsel is looking for explicit wording around prompt/response attribution — they want to confirm that outputs we receive are not claimed by Redwood as model IP and that we retain rights to prompts and responses for our product. Can you share the redline-friendly clause wording you recommend?

2) Subprocessor map + dataflow: we need a clear inventory of subprocessors that touch prompt/response artifacts (including analytics, logging, or telemetry) and a dataflow diagram showing where prompt/response material is stored, for how long, and where it might transit across regions. SOC 2 evidence will be requested if anything is stored outside our EU/US boundary.

If you can attach a simple map and a one-page attestation on no-training/no-derivative-claims for our review, that would help accelerate sign-off. Samir (copied) is the legal lead and will coordinate edits.

Best,
Maria
Director, Product Compliance
MedScale Health

Attachments: none in this message

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@medscale.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@medscale.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify attribution + subprocessor map for DPA review

Hi Maria / Samir,

Appreciate the clear asks — happy to get this over. Quick notes up-front: Redwood’s standard DPA includes an explicit "no-claim on customer prompts/responses" clause and a training-exclusion attestation option for customers who require it. For MedScale we can:

- Provide a redline with a short attribution paragraph you can paste into your DPA (I'll attach a suggested clause).
- Share a high-level subprocessor inventory and a minimal dataflow map (what touches logs, KV cache, telemetry).
- Produce a one-page attestation confirming we will not use MedScale prompts/responses to improve our public models and will treat prompt/response artifacts per the residency and retention commitments you specify.

Action plan: I’ll drop a dataflow PDF and the clause text in a follow-up email. Marissa — can you flag any export-control/residency constraints we should bake into the attestation? Dev — please include the current list of subprocessors and the evidence manifest (SOC/SLA docs).

Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Partnerships (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dataflow_map_v1.pdf (attached in follow-up)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, Maria Santos <maria.santos@medscale.ai>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, Samir Patel <samir@medscale.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify attribution + subprocessor map for DPA review

Thanks — adding a couple of pragmatic constraints we typically see with healthcare customers:

- Residency: If MedScale requires EU-only residency for prompt/response storage, we can toggle routing (edge/region pins) but some telemetry (aggregated, non-identifiable) may still be stored for operational metrics. We will clearly mark that in the map.
- Retention: We can offer a 30 / 90 / custom retention policy for prompt logs and provide an export on request.
- Export controls / backups: note that backups and cross-region replication are disabled when region-pin is enabled; we will state that explicitly in the attestation.

I’ve reviewed the draft dataflow and added notes to page 2 about KV cache lifetimes and where ephemeral cache persists. Happy to sync quickly if you want to walk through it.

-Marissa Cole
Sr. PM, Redwood Console

Hi all,

Attached are the requested artifacts: dataflow_map_v1.pdf, a redline named dpa_redline_medscale.docx with the proposed attribution and training-exclusion text, and an evidence_manifest.csv that points to our SOC/Security attestations. Highlights:

- "Attribution/Ownership" clause (proposed): Redwood does not claim ownership of customer-provided prompts or customer-obtained model responses. Customer retains rights to prompts, inputs, outputs, and any derivative product they create from outputs unless otherwise agreed in writing.

- "Training exclusion" attestation (proposed): Redwood will not use MedScale prompt/response data to train, fine-tune, or improve any Redwood-hosted public models. For Dedicated or Private deployments where customers opt-in to shared telemetry, separate terms would apply.

- Subprocessors: current list included (analytics vendor, monitoring vendor, cloud infra provider). The manifest includes links to SOC 2 Type II reports where available.

Next steps: Jonas / Samir — if the clause wording looks good I can incorporate any legal edits, and we can produce a one-page signed attestation document for your records.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
